title: 2026 Solar Eclipse in Ticino: the power of the Sun and how to protect yourself | VAM Deco
description: The eclipse of 12 August 2026 covered 92% of the Sun over Ticino. A reminder to protect your home, shop and car from UV rays and heat, all year round.
h1: 2026 Solar Eclipse: the power of the Sun seen from Ticino
coverCredito: Cover photo: Vishnu Narippatta, Wikimedia Commons (CC BY-SA 4.0).
estratto: The eclipse of 12 August reminded everyone of the power of the Sun. But the Sun pours through every window, every day: here's how to protect your home, shop and car.

paragrafi: On 12 August 2026, the sky over Ticino put on a rare show: a partial solar eclipse. At its peak, around 8:17 p.m., the Moon covered roughly 92% of the Sun (91.83% in Lugano at 8:19 p.m.). A captivating sight, and a reminder of just how much energy the Sun pours onto us every single day.

Watching it safely required certified glasses. But the Sun doesn't only reach us during an eclipse: it passes through every window in your home, office, shop and car, all year long. And that's exactly where protection becomes an everyday matter.

sezioni.heading: Watching the Sun: your eyes always need protecting
paragrafi: Looking at the Sun with the naked eye, even when it's 92% covered, can seriously damage your retina. To watch an eclipse safely you need glasses certified to the ISO 12312-2 standard: sunglasses won't do, nor will smoked glass or a window film.
This is an important point to make clear: the solar films we apply to windows are there to protect spaces and people from the everyday Sun, not to look directly at it. They are two different things.

sezioni.heading: The Sun comes through every window, all year round
paragrafi: Even without an eclipse, the Sun's rays pass through every glazed surface. UV rays fade furniture, fabrics, parquet and displays; the heat turns an office or a car's interior into a greenhouse; direct light causes glare and tires your eyes.

In Ticino, with summers getting hotter, this is a real problem for homes, shops, offices and vehicles. A good solar film works quietly 365 days a year, cutting heat and harmful rays without taking away the light.

faq.domanda: Can I watch the eclipse through a window film or a tinted car window?
faq.risposta: No, absolutely not. To watch the Sun safely you need ISO 12312-2 certified glasses. Window films and tinted car windows don't provide the protection your eyes need: they're designed to protect spaces from the Sun, not to look directly at it.

faq.domanda: How much heat and how many UV rays do solar control films block?
faq.risposta: Professional films block up to 99% of UV rays and a significant share of the Sun's heat, lowering the indoor temperature and protecting furnishings and fabrics, all without giving up natural light.

faq.domanda: Is car window tinting allowed in Switzerland?
faq.risposta: The rear side windows and the rear windscreen can be tinted. For the windscreen and front windows, Swiss law sets precise limits: we always propose compliant solutions. When we prepare your quote, we assess together what's permitted on your vehicle.

faq.domanda: Do films damage the glass? Can they be removed?
faq.risposta: No. Professional films don't damage the glass and can be removed or replaced in the future, leaving no residue when applied correctly.

faq.domanda: Do you apply films to shop windows and offices too, not just cars?
faq.risposta: Yes. We handle glazing for homes, offices and shops with solar control films and UV window tinting, as well as car window tinting, throughout Ticino.
